celestial_objects.name: Sun
celestial_objects.description: The central star of our solar system. Highly unrecommended as a landing spot.
fun_facts: Contains 99.86% of the mass in the Solar System
Over 1 million Earths could fit inside the Sun
Surface temperature is around 5,500°C

celestial_objects.name: Mercury
celestial_objects.description: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun, with extreme temperature swings.
fun_facts: A year on Mercury is only 88 Earth days
Mercury has extreme temperature swings in the solar system
A day on Mercury lasts 59 Earth days

celestial_objects.name: Venus
celestial_objects.description: The hottest planet with a thick toxic atmosphere and crushing pressure.
fun_facts: Venus rotates backwards compared to most planets
A day on Venus is longer than its year
Surface temperature can melt lead

celestial_objects.name: Earth
celestial_objects.description: Our home planet, the only known world with liquid water on its surface.
fun_facts: Earth is the only planet not named after a god
71% of Earth's surface is covered by water
Earth's rotation is gradually slowing down

celestial_objects.name: Moon
celestial_objects.description: Earth's natural satellite, site of humanity's first footsteps beyond Earth.
fun_facts: The Moon is moving away from Earth at 3.8 cm per year
Moonquakes occur regularly on the lunar surface
Gravity on the Moon is 1/6th of Earth's gravity

celestial_objects.name: Mars
celestial_objects.description: The Red Planet, a cold desert world with the largest volcano in the solar system.
fun_facts: Olympus Mons on Mars is 3x taller than Mt. Everest
Mars has the largest dust storms in the solar system
A day on Mars is called a 'sol'

celestial_objects.name: Ceres
celestial_objects.description: The largest object in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
fun_facts: Ceres accounts for 1/3rd of the total mass of the main asteroid belt
Contains large amounts of water ice under its crust
First dwarf planet visited by a spacecraft (Dawn)

celestial_objects.name: Jupiter
celestial_objects.description: The largest planet, a gas giant with a famous Great Red Spot storm.
fun_facts: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth
Jupiter has the shortest day of all planets
Acts as a cosmic vacuum cleaner protecting inner planets

celestial_objects.name: Saturn
celestial_objects.description: The ringed planet, famous for its spectacular ring system made of ice and rock.
fun_facts: Saturn's rings are mostly made of ice particles
Saturn is the least dense planet - it would float in water
Saturn has 146 known moons

celestial_objects.name: Uranus
celestial_objects.description: An ice giant that rotates on its side, with faint rings.
fun_facts: Uranus rotates on its side due to an ancient collision
Coldest planetary atmosphere in the solar system
First planet discovered using a telescope

celestial_objects.name: Neptune
celestial_objects.description: The windiest planet, an ice giant with the strongest sustained winds.
fun_facts: Strongest sustained winds in the solar system (2,100 km/h)
Predicted mathematically before being observed
A year on Neptune lasts 165 Earth years

celestial_objects.name: Pluto
celestial_objects.description: A dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt with a heart-shaped nitrogen glacier.
fun_facts: Reclassified from planet to dwarf planet in 2006
Has a heart-shaped glacier called Tombaugh Regio
Charon moon is half Pluto's size

celestial_objects.name: Halley's Comet
celestial_objects.description: The most famous periodic comet, returning to inner solar system every 75-76 years.
fun_facts: Returns to inner solar system every 75-76 years
Composed of volatile ice, dust, and rock
Next perihelion will be in mid-2061
